messages:
Alice K.: customer report: Next.js app (edge runtime) using @redwood/inference from a page bundle gets 403 "Missing Authorization header" when hitting hosted API. Server-side calls succeed. They sent a tiny repro and network logs.

Ben S.: ok can you paste the repro and the devtools network trace? is the request originating from the browser or from an edge function?

Alice K.: it's from a client-side page that uses the edge runtime. snippet they provided:

```ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RW_KEY })
await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })
```

Network: OPTIONS preflight returns 204; the POST then returns 403 with body {"error":"authorization header missing"}.

Carlos M.: couple of immediate flags: (1) putting secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC is unsafe, (2) browsers will drop Authorization on cross-origin POSTs unless CORS preflight allows that header. Which SDK version? older bundling can also mangle fetch behavior.

Alice K.: they are on @redwood/inference@0.8.0. they also tried manually setting headers in fetch and still saw 403.

Diana R.: v0.8 had Node-first bundling that sometimes relied on server global headers paths. We shipped an explicit browser/edge build in 0.9.0 that fixes header handling and reduces bundle size. Recommend upgrade to 0.9.x. Also verify the API's OPTIONS response includes Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization. Without that the browser will not send the header on the real request.

Ben S.: repro I tried locally: Next edge bundle (v0.8) ends up with the Authorization header present in JS but the browser refuses to send it because the preflight didn't advertise it. Vercel's CDN/edge isn't stripping headers by default, but the browser enforces CORS. Ensure OPTIONS replies include: Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, and Access-Control-Allow-Methods.

Alice K.: customer also tried Cloudflare Workers and saw similar symptoms. In CF Worker outbound fetch you can set headers, but if the request originates from user-agent and the API doesn't allow Authorization via CORS, the browser will block sending it. So it's consistent.

Diana R.: recommended troubleshooting steps I emailed them: 
- Do not expose long-lived API keys in NEXT_PUBLIC. Instead, use a server/edge route to mint short-lived client tokens or proxy calls.
- Upgrade SDK to >=0.9.2 for browser/edge-safe bundle.
- Verify API CORS: OPTIONS must respond with Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type and Access-Control-Allow-Origin matching the requesting origin.
- If calling from an edge function (Vercel Edge Fn) that can hold secrets, prefer calling hosted API from that Edge Fn rather than the end user's browser.

Carlos M.: added a tiny browser check they can run to validate CORS preflight: 

```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/test', { method: 'OPTIONS', mode: 'cors', headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer x' } })
  .then(r => { console.log('cors headers:', Array.from(r.headers.entries())); })
  .catch(e => console.error('preflight failed', e));
```

If the response doesn't include access-control-allow-headers: Authorization, the browser will not send Authorization for the POST.

Alice K.: customer confirmed their OPTIONS lacked the header. They upgraded to 0.9.2 and implemented a small edge-proxy that mints ephemeral tokens from a server-side secret. After that, calls succeeded and 403 stopped.

infra-bot: created RW-8942 to add a KB and example edge proxy for Next.js (Vercel) and Cloudflare Workers.

Ben S.: can someone add a minimal doc snippet for browser -> edge-proxy -> hosted API? I'll review once drafted.

Diana R.: I'll draft it: include the CORS checklist, the preflight diagnostic snippet, and recommended SDK version range. Also call out the security risk of shipping secrets in public bundles.

Alice K.: thank you all :thumbsup: marking the case resolved; will follow-up with the customer notes and link to RW-8942.
